comparison: Both evaluate claims about the αC-β4 loop as a conserved structural motif (C1, C2, C24-26, C48-51, C56). OpenEval finds the structural evidence well-documented and SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers also find this SUPPORTED, acknowledging the loop as a 'previously overlooked structural motif' and the study as 'valuable.' OpenEval includes C52-55 which peer review also covers but groups separately.

Perfect match on claims C5, C91, C92 regarding F100A mutation's biochemical effects. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the claims are explicitly stated with citation and provide clear functional evidence. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge this as established prior work that motivates the computational analyses.

Perfect match on LSP analysis claims (C6, C9, C10, C106-123). OpenEval finds the LSP results SUPPORTED with coherent quantitative centrality measures. Peer reviewers rate this UNCERTAIN, acknowledging the data are 'intriguing and mostly solid' but stating 'further analysis and additional experiments will be needed' and that findings are insufficient on their own.
